issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature differs between artifacts: the problem statement (and the template Main usage) specify a no-argument method messageOnRide(): String, but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementations (Pig, Seal) also require an int parameter. This parameter mismatch prevents students from implementing the exercise as described and makes the provided Main/template code incompatible with the solution's interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide method signature consistent with the problem statement and template by removing the int parameter: define messageOnRide(): String in Rideable, and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning the string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if the speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement and the template Main usage to reflect messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust example calls accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a parameterless method messageOnRide() on the Rideable interface (used as r.messageOnRide()), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it in Pig and Seal with an int parameter. This mismatched method signature (and the changed return wording including speed) creates a direct mapping conflict: students following the problem/template will implement or call messageOnRide() with no arguments, while the solution uses a different identifier/signature, causing confusion and likely compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable interface and its implementations with the problem/template by changing the solution's Rideable method signature to: String messageOnRide(); and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() (no parameters) returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if speed is intended, update the problem statement and template call sites to require and pass an int parameter, but the simpler fix is to make the solution match the parameterless design in the problem/template.
